transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I guess the main thing is work meetings. I’m in advertising sales, so we have these long strategy meetings, and I know I’m supposed to just sit there and listen, but I keep getting up—like to refill my water, or I’ll end up pacing near the printer for a minute. It sounds kind of silly saying it out loud, because everyone gets restless, right? But it’s been noticeable enough that I thought maybe I should talk to someone about it.
Have you noticed this kind of restlessness and difficulty sitting still since you were a child, or is this something that started more recently as an adult?

No, it definitely goes back. I mean, I don’t remember thinking of it as “restlessness” back then, but in elementary school my teachers would write stuff like I was bright but rushed through things, talked out of turn, forgot homework… and my desk was always this disaster, like stuffed with half-finished papers. My mom used to make me clean it out and I’d find worksheets from weeks before. So, yeah, it wasn’t just something that suddenly started with work.

When you notice yourself needing to get up and move during meetings, is it usually accompanied by a lot of worried or anxious thoughts running through your mind, or does it happen even when you're not particularly worried about anything?

It happens even when I’m not especially worried. Like, the big thing is those long sales strategy meetings—I know I’m supposed to stay seated, but I’ll just feel like I have to get up, refill my water, or I’ll wander over by the printer and kind of pace for a minute. Sometimes I’m thinking about the meeting, sometimes I’m not thinking about much at all. It’s not always, like, anxiety driving it.
Aside from the restlessness, do you currently notice problems like losing focus during tasks, forgetting things, or losing track of items you need for work?

Yeah, focus is definitely an issue. Like in longer strategy meetings, I’ll start out really trying to follow along, and then a few minutes later I realize I’ve just been staring at the same slide and I don’t actually know what the last point was.

It happens when I’m reading client briefs too. I’ll be looking at a paragraph, and then I’m like, wait, did I read that? And I have to go back. Which is annoying because some of those briefs are already kind of dense and full of buzzwords, and then I start thinking about how we’re going to pitch it, or what the client really means by “brand authenticity,” and then I realize I’ve completely stopped absorbing the actual text.
Do you often find yourself interrupting others, blurting out responses before someone finishes speaking, or having trouble waiting your turn in conversations or meetings?

Yeah, I do that. I’ll jump in with an answer before the person’s even finished the question—especially with clients or coworkers—because I think I know where they’re going with it. And then two seconds later I realize, oh, that wasn’t actually what they were asking, or I kind of cut them off.

It’s embarrassing, honestly. Sometimes in meetings I’m trying to look engaged and quick, and then I end up answering the wrong thing because I didn’t let them finish.

Do you notice this same kind of restlessness, distractibility, or impulsivity in other parts of your life outside of work—like at home, during conversations with friends or family, or when you're doing personal tasks?

I’m not totally sure. I mean, I probably do sometimes, but I haven’t really tracked it outside of work the same way. Work is just where it’s most obvious because there are meetings and people notice.

At home it’s more like… I’ll start doing something and then end up doing three other little things, but I don’t know if that’s the same thing or just normal. And with friends, I try not to interrupt, though I’m sure I’ve done it. Sorry, I’m kind of thinking of random examples now. I guess I’d say I haven’t noticed it as clearly outside work.

Thinking specifically about home—like paying bills, managing chores, or following through on personal projects—do you find yourself losing focus, leaving tasks unfinished, or feeling restless in the same way you do at work?

At home, I’m honestly not sure I can give a clean example. I don’t want to overstate it.

The clearest version I notice is still with work stuff, like I’ll get almost all of a proposal done or update most of something in the CRM, and then somehow leave off the very last step—sending the final version, or logging the follow-up—even though I fully meant to finish it. It’s not like I decided not to do it, it’s more like I mentally moved on too early.

So… at home, maybe it happens, but I’m having a harder time pinning down a specific example. The follow-through issue is definitely easier for me to see with work tasks.
Can you tell me about a specific example of paying bills or handling personal paperwork at home—do you ever miss due dates, forget to finish the process, or lose track of the task partway through?

With bills or personal paperwork, I’m trying to think of a really specific example and I’m blanking a little. I don’t want to say I’m constantly missing due dates if I’m not sure.

The thing that’s most like that, though, is at work—like I’ll get almost all the way through a proposal or a CRM update, and then somehow not do the final step. Like I’ll forget to send the final version, or I won’t log the follow-up even though that was the whole point. And it’s not that I didn’t care or decided to skip it, I just kind of mentally move on before it’s actually finished.

At home, I guess it might happen with paperwork too, but I’m having trouble pulling up a clean example right now.

Outside of work, do you notice these issues affecting things like your social life or hobbies—for example, losing focus during conversations, forgetting plans, or feeling restless during activities you enjoy, like watching a movie or being at a social gathering?

With social stuff, I’m not sure I notice it as much as at work. I mean, if I’m with friends I can usually follow along, unless it’s a loud place or something, but that feels kind of normal.

The clearer thing is when someone is talking directly to me at work—like my manager giving me feedback, or a client explaining what they want changed. I’ll be looking right at them, nodding, like I’m listening, and then a few seconds later I realize I missed a key part and I have to ask them to repeat it. Which is embarrassing, because it looks like I wasn’t paying attention even though I thought I was.

Outside work, maybe it happens in conversations too, but I can’t think of a super clean example right now.
When you're driving, do you notice similar issues—like feeling restless, making impulsive decisions (such as cutting people off or changing lanes quickly), or losing focus and missing turns or exits?

Driving… I don’t know, I’m not sure I’d say that’s the main place I notice it. I don’t really have a clear example of cutting people off or anything like that.

The thing it reminds me of more is when I’m in longer strategy meetings, or even reading a client brief. I’ll start off focused, like I’m genuinely trying to follow it, and then a few minutes later I realize I’ve been staring at the same slide or the same paragraph and I don’t actually know what the last point was. Then I have to kind of backtrack mentally, or reread it.

So with driving, I’m not sure. Maybe it’s not as obvious there. But that “I was looking at it and somehow didn’t take it in” thing definitely happens with meetings and briefs.

Have you ever been told by a partner, roommate, or family member that you seem distracted, restless, or forget things around the house—like household responsibilities or commitments you've made to them?

I mean… not so much around the house that I can give you a perfect example. My partner has said I seem like I “leave things unfinished,” but when I think of the clearest version of that, it’s honestly more work stuff again.

Like I’ll do almost all of a proposal or a CRM update, and in my head it feels basically done, but then I leave off the last step—sending the final version, or logging the follow-up. And that’s the part that actually matters. I meant to finish it, I didn’t decide not to, I just sort of move on mentally before I close the loop.

At home it’s probably similar with little responsibilities, but I’m having trouble naming one clean example.

Outside of work, do you notice yourself fidgeting, tapping your leg, talking more than others, or feeling like you need to keep moving—for example, during a long dinner, a movie, or just relaxing at home?

Yeah, I mean… I don’t know if I’d say I’m super fidgety at home during a movie or dinner. Maybe a little, but that’s not the thing that made me think, “Okay, this is a problem.”

Honestly, what made me come in is more that in long sales strategy meetings, I keep getting up when I know I’m supposed to stay seated. Like I’ll tell myself I’m just refilling my water, or I need to check something by the printer, but really I think I just can’t sit there the whole time. And then I worry it looks rude or like I’m not taking the meeting seriously, even though I am trying to.

Can you think of a specific hobby or personal project—like reading a book, doing a home repair, or something similar—where you've noticed yourself losing focus, leaving it unfinished, or feeling restless in the middle of it?

Yeah, I’m trying to think of a hobby example, and I’m sort of blanking on a clean one. Like I’ll start a book sometimes and then suddenly realize I’ve reread the same page, but the place I really notice it is still more with work reading.

Like with a client brief, I’ll sit down meaning to really absorb it, and I’m looking right at the paragraph, but a few minutes later I realize I have no idea what I just read. Same with strategy meetings — I’ll be staring at the slide, nodding along, and then I’m like, wait, what was the last point? Then I have to go back or ask myself what I missed, which is kind of embarrassing.
Thinking about just the past week, can you recall a specific non-work task—like paying a bill, replying to a personal text, or finishing a chore—that you started but didn't complete?

This past week… I’m trying to think of a non-work one, like an actual bill or text, but the clearest thing that comes to mind is still work-adjacent. Sorry, I know you asked non-work.

It’s that same pattern where I’ll get almost all of something done, like a proposal or a CRM update, and then somehow I don’t do the final step. Like I’ll have the proposal basically ready but not send the final version, or I’ll mean to log the follow-up and then just… don’t close it out. In my head it feels finished, even though technically the important last piece isn’t done.
